Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following discipline for comparing the model with recorded data.

**(i) Declared model of each comparison.** A comparison of a model prediction with an experiment of the framework requires, in addition to the state and dynamics assumptions P1-P5, the following declared items: a **preparation model**, that is, a specification of the state or preparation assigned to the system together with the physical procedure that realizes it; an **isolation model**, that is, the energy operator used and a statement of the interactions neglected in the approximation; a **detection model**, that is, the response of the apparatus, including efficiency, resolution, background and any binning; and **sampling assumptions**, that is, the statistical model under which repetitions of the preparation and detection are combined. None of these items is supplied by the mathematical framework alone.

**(ii) Repetitions.** The treatment of repeated trials as independent and identically distributed draws from the model's outcome law is an additional statistical model of the apparatus and the procedure. It is not a consequence of the state postulate and is not guaranteed by the mathematics; where it is assumed it is stated, and where it fails (correlated trials, drifting preparation, dead time, selection) the statistical analysis must model the departure or record the limitation.

**(iii) Identification with uncertainty.** The claim "this apparatus realizes the preparation $\rho$ and the dynamics $H_{\mathrm{op}}$" and the claim "this detector realizes the effect $F$" are physical identifications: they are tested against recorded behaviour of the apparatus, carry uncertainty and can fail. They are not derived from the framework, and a model prediction obtained under them inherits their qualifications. Calibration procedures, control experiments and their limitations are recorded with the comparison.

**(iv) Empirical premises.** Where a measured value enters a deduction - a mass, a charge, a field strength, a detector efficiency - it enters as a qualified empirical premise with its uncertainty, conditions of measurement and source, and the conclusion of the deduction carries those qualifications. A deduction that uses a measured input is not an exact statement about nature.

**(v) Status.** Clauses (i)-(iv) are adopted as the framework's conditions for comparing model with data. They make no claim that the framework or the apparatus description is exact; agreement of a prediction with a dataset is evidence about the combined model and apparatus assumptions, not a proof of the framework and not a statement about nature deduced from the mathematics.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework, for systems in the declared massive-matter sector, the following statements about states and their composition. Assume throughout the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is the choice hypothesis of the mathematical suppliers cited below.

**(i) State space.** To each physical system of the sector the model assigns a complex Hilbert space $H$ that is nonzero and separable: a complex Hilbert space in the sense of [[def-hilbert-space]] which admits a sequence whose range is dense in $H$, so that the hypothesis of [[thm-separable-hilbert-space-has-a-countable-orthonormal-basis]] holds and $H$ has a finite or countable orthonormal basis. The assignment of a Hilbert space to a physical system is a model assumption; the linear structure used to combine descriptions mathematically is not an empirical claim. The physical system to which $H$ is assigned, and the sector in which the assignment is made, are declared with it.

**(ii) Pure preparations.** A **pure preparation** of the system is a unit ray $[\psi]=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a vector $\psi\in H$ with $\|\psi\|=1$; that is, two nonzero vectors describe the same pure preparation exactly when they differ by a nonzero complex factor. The zero vector is not a state and no preparation is assigned to it: the normalization $\|\psi\|=1$ is part of the assignment. The ray allows arbitrary nonzero rescaling; between unit representatives the factor has modulus one and is a **global phase**, which has no observable consequence (P2). The rank-one operator $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] is the density operator associated with the ray of $\psi$.

**(iii) General preparations and mixing.** A general preparation of the system is a **density operator**: a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ on $H$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)). Pure preparations are the special case $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ with $\|\psi\|=1$. A **statistical mixture** of preparations $\rho_{n}$ with weights $w_{n}\ge0$, $\sum_{n}w_{n}=1$, is the trace-norm convergent sum $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ as follows directly in the trace-class Banach space ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]): each density has trace norm one, so $\sum_n\|w_n\rho_n\|_1=1$ gives trace-norm convergence. Every partial sum is positive; operator-norm convergence preserves its nonnegative quadratic forms, and continuity of trace gives $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). Thus the limit is again a density operator, without requiring the components to be orthogonal pure states. The weights are a classical preparation uncertainty and are not amplitudes. Distinct weighted ensembles of pure states may define the same $\rho$.

**(iv) Composition.** Two independent distinguishable subsystems with state spaces $H_{A}$ and $H_{B}$ are composed by the completed Hilbert tensor product $H_{A}\widehat\otimes H_{B}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. Product preparations $\psi_{A}\otimes\psi_{B}$ are the special case of preparations in which each subsystem has its own specified preparation; general composite preparations are linear combinations and mixtures and need not factor. A quantity of subsystem $A$ alone is represented on the composite by an operator of the form $A\otimes I_{B}$ and a quantity of $B$ alone by $I_{A}\otimes B$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] (bounded case; unbounded local operators are treated where they occur). The existence of the completed tensor product is mathematics; the assignment of that product to a composite physical system is the physical assumption here.

**(v) Restrictions that are separate assumptions.** Restrictions of the state space by superselection rules, identical-particle symmetry sectors, and the replacement of the tensor product by more general algebraic structures are not consequences of the clauses above: where such a restriction is used it is adopted separately, and the identical-species sectors are the subject of the postulate P6 of this page.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model within its declared sector. They are not derived from experiment, and they do not assert that a physical system is exactly described by such a Hilbert space; no numerical measurement is recorded. The compatibility of the framework with observation is a question about fully specified models and reported data, in the sense of P7.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following statements about sharp and unsharp real-valued quantities. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The latter is the explicit hypothesis used to obtain the spectral PVM of a general self-adjoint operator from [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] in clause (ii); consumers invoking this construction inherit it.

**(i) Sharp observables.** An **ideal sharp real-valued quantity** (observable) of a system with state space $H$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), together with a declared unit in which its real spectral coordinate is read; the unit is part of the assignment, and no numerical value of the coordinate is asserted by the assignment. Symmetry of $A$ on a small domain is not sufficient for self-adjointness, and the domain is a declared part of the observable.

**(ii) Spectral probability.** Let $E_{A}$ be the spectral projection-valued measure of the self-adjoint operator $A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$ and a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ the **probability of the outcome in $B$** is
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_{A}(B)\bigr),\qquad\text{and for a pure preparation }[\psi]\text{ it is }\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}.$$
By clause (b) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] the assignment $B\mapsto\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$ is a probability measure on the Borel sets ([[def-probability-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). It is the general form of the Born rule adopted here.

**(iii) Nature of the outcome law.** The probability law is a measure, not necessarily a density with respect to Lebesgue measure and not necessarily a finite or countable sum of point masses: a self-adjoint operator with continuous spectrum ordinarily has no normalizable eigenvector at a point of its continuous spectrum, so an "exact value" of a continuum quantity is not represented by a normalized state. An ideal point value is an idealization; a real detector reports a finite-resolution outcome, that is, the probability of a declared Borel set $B$ such as a bin, and the recorded-event probability is that of (ii) for the bin, not the value of a density at a point.

**(iv) Unsharp finite outcomes.** Outcomes of a finite-resolution apparatus with finitely many channels are described, when the idealization uses bounded effects, by a finite family $(F_{a})_{a=1}^{p}$ of bounded operators with $0\le F_{a}\le I$ in the quadratic-form order and $\sum_{a}F_{a}=I$ ([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (a)), the **outcome probabilities** being $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})\ge0$, $\sum_{a}p_{a}=1$ by clause (b) of the same lemma. This unsharp extension is an operational description tied to an apparatus model; it is not obtained from the sharp observable by mathematical manipulation alone, and the effects alone do not determine what happens to the state after the outcome (P3).

**(v) Moments are a separate matter.** Statements about the mean, variance or higher moments of the outcome law require the corresponding integrability of $t\mapsto t^{n}$ against $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ and are not part of this postulate; where they are used they are stated with their hypotheses. In particular the existence of $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$ for an unbounded $A$ is not asserted.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model. They assert nothing about which quantities of a concrete apparatus are sharp, about the physical mechanism producing an outcome or about the completeness of the description; a laboratory record is a classical event whose relation to the model is a tested identification with uncertainty, in the sense of P7.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

## Scope of the examples page

**What the three items establish.**
[[ex-nrqm-light-matter-two-level-dipole-drive-check]] identifies declared
two-level Pauli matter data with the linear two-level drive model of the
driven-dynamics page, computes the resonant co-rotating first-order amplitude
and shows that its probability is the leading term of the exact averaged Rabi
probability of that model.
[[ex-nrqm-light-matter-hydrogen-dipole-angular-factors]] computes explicit
angular factors of the hydrogenic dipole matrix elements — $1/\sqrt3$ for the
allowed $1s$-to-$2p$ and $2p$-to-$1s$ angular entries, and zero for the
forbidden $1s$-to-$1s$, $1s$-to-$2s$ and $m$-violating entries — together with
the oscillator contrast $|\Delta n|=1$.
[[texp-nrqm-light-matter-spectral-density-and-detected-photon-comparison]]
proves that two declared cutoff-dipole models whose mode densities agree at
the transition energy have the same rate coefficient but different
detected-photon energy laws at every finite time, and that a declared
sharp-line model is the idealisation approached in the limit rather than a
property of the finite-time law.

**What they rest on.** All three are conditional on the state and composition
postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the preparation
and apparatus discipline P7 in the readings of the model
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]], on the
spectral-transition reading
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]], on the
single-vertex mathematics [[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]]
and on the main-page results [[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-stimulated-dipole-drive-transitions]],
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-dipole-selection-rules]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-golden-rule-limit-and-rate-reading]]. The two-level
example's parameters $\omega_{0},d,E_{0},\omega$ and the densities
$J_{1},J_{2}$ are declared model data, not measured values.

**What is not claimed.** The page records no experiment, no apparatus, no
calibration, no count, no frequency, no efficiency and no uncertainty budget,
and none is invented. It does not claim that any laboratory atom, field,
spectrometer or detector realizes the declared models; those are tested
identifications with uncertainty under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). It asserts no rate,
lifetime, linewidth or exponential decay from any of its comparisons, and no
statistical inference. Comparing the declared model laws with data would test
the combined model and apparatus assumptions under a declared sampling and
measurement model, would carry finite-sample fluctuations, selection effects
and systematic uncertainties, and would not prove a model; spectra, counts
and lifetimes remain research candidates for a separate reported-experiment
item, and energy differences or successful comparisons alone do not establish
that the framework is a proof of nature.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\hbar>0$.

**(a) The golden-rule kernel.** For $t>0$ define
$$K_t(x):=\frac1{\hbar^2t}\Bigl|\int_0^te^{ixs/\hbar}\,ds\Bigr|^2,\qquad x\in\mathbb R .$$
Then $K_t$ is continuous, nonnegative and even, and for $x\ne0$
$$K_t(x)=\frac{4\sin^2\bigl(xt/(2\hbar)\bigr)}{x^2t},\qquad K_t(0)=\frac t{\hbar^2};$$
moreover for every $\delta>0$ and every $x$ with $|x|\ge\delta$,
$$K_t(x)\le\frac4{x^2t}\le\frac4{\delta^2t},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}K_t(x)\,dx=\frac{2\pi}{\hbar}.$$

**(b) Approximate identity.** Let $J\in L^1(\mathbb R)$
([[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]) and let $\Delta\in\mathbb R$.
If the representative $J$ is continuous at $\Delta$
([[def-continuity-real]]), then
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\int_{\mathbb R}K_t(x)J(\Delta+x)\,dx=\frac{2\pi}{\hbar}J(\Delta)$$
([[def-limits-at-infinity]]).

**(c) First-order emission coefficient.** Adopt the objects and hypotheses of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]]: $\alpha>0$, the
transverse space $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_\Pi$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
with $\varepsilon(k)=\alpha|k|$, the cutoff $\Lambda>0$, the vectors
$g_1,\dots,g_J\in\mathfrak h$ ($J\ge1$) with
$$\operatorname{supp}g_j\subseteq\{k:\ 0<\varepsilon(k)\le\Lambda\},\qquad \frac{g_j}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\in\mathfrak h,$$
the Hermitian $d\times d$ matrices $H_a,D_1,\dots,D_J$ and the coupling
$\eta_0\in\mathbb R$. Let $v_a,v_b$ be orthonormal eigenvectors of $H_a$ with
$H_av_a=E_av_a$, $H_av_b=E_av_b$, and let $\Delta:=E_a-E_b>0$. Put

**(i) State space.** To each physical system of the sector the model assigns a complex Hilbert space $H$ that is nonzero and separable: a complex Hilbert space in the sense of [[def-hilbert-space]] which admits a sequence whose range is dense in $H$, so that the hypothesis of [[thm-separable-hilbert-space-has-a-countable-orthonormal-basis]] holds and $H$ has a finite or countable orthonormal basis. The physical system to which $H$ is assigned, and the sector in which the assignment is made, are declared with it.

**(ii) Pure preparations.** A **pure preparation** of the system is a unit ray $[\psi]=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a vector $\psi\in H$ with $\|\psi\|=1$; that is, two nonzero vectors describe the same pure preparation exactly when they differ by a nonzero complex factor. The zero vector is not a state and no preparation is assigned to it: the normalization $\|\psi\|=1$ is part of the assignment. The ray allows arbitrary nonzero rescaling; between unit representatives the factor has modulus one and is a **global phase**, which has no observable consequence (P2). The rank-one operator $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] is the density operator associated with the ray of $\psi$.

**(iii) General preparations and mixing.** A general preparation of the system is a **density operator**: a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ on $H$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)). Pure preparations are the special case $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ with $\|\psi\|=1$. A **statistical mixture** of preparations $\rho_{n}$ with weights $w_{n}\ge0$, $\sum_{n}w_{n}=1$, is the trace-norm convergent sum $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ as follows directly in the trace-class Banach space ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]): each density has trace norm one, so $\sum_n\|w_n\rho_n\|_1=1$ gives trace-norm convergence. Every partial sum is positive; operator-norm convergence preserves its nonnegative quadratic forms, and continuity of trace gives $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). A quantity of subsystem $A$ alone is represented on the composite by an operator of the form $A\otimes I_{B}$ and a quantity of $B$ alone by $I_{A}\otimes B$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] (bounded case; unbounded local operators are treated where they occur). Consumer def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model raw cd287345387d1b6129c61d05bf31af54edad297439c7fddaf9c0d4b936d3c211; supplier def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity raw ed58365c34df607cd851a042b2cd9013c1755e0da68a20788628d2919a55f14b; current facts no fact paragraph pairing (declared context); exact Definition:
**Density operators.** Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space. A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a) ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). The **state space** of $H$ is the set of all density operators on $H$ and is denoted
$$D(H):=\{\rho:\rho\ \text{is a density operator on}\ H\}.$$
An element of $D(H)$ is called a **state** of $H$ in the mathematical sense fixed here.

**Pure states.** A state $\rho\in D(H)$ is **pure** when there is a unit vector $u\in S(H)$ with
$$\rho=T_{u,u},\qquad T_{u,u}x=\langle x,u\rangle u\quad(x\in H),$$
where $T_{u,u}$ is the rank-one operator of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] and $S(H)$ is the unit sphere of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the pure states are exactly the Hilbert orthogonal projections of $H$ with one-dimensional range, and the map
$$j:R(H)\longrightarrow D(H),\qquad j([\psi]):=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)},$$
on the ray space $R(H)$, with $\nu$ the normalization map, is well defined and injective with image the set of pure states. A state is **mixed** when it is not pure. For a nonzero vector $\psi$ the **normalized rank-one operator of $\psi$** is
$$\widehat\rho(\psi):=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,\psi})},$$
which equals $T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)}$; thus $\widehat\rho(\psi)$ is the pure state of the ray $[\psi]$, and the vector $\psi$ enters only through its ray.

**Purity.** For $\rho\in D(H)$ the operator $\rho^{2}$ is self-adjoint, positive and trace class: it is self-adjoint by the adjoint algebra of [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], positive because $\langle\rho^{2}x,x\rangle=\langle\rho x,\rho x\rangle\ge0$, and trace class because $\rho$ is a bounded trace-class operator and the trace-class operators form a two-sided ideal ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clauses 1 and 2). The **purity** of $\rho$ is the real number
$$\mathcal P(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2})\in\mathbb R.$$
The numerical range of the purity and the equivalence of purity with purity of the state are established by the purity criterion of this page; this definition records the object only.

**Scope.** This definition fixes the mathematical state space of a Hilbert space together with the pure states, the mixed states, the normalized rank-one operator of a nonzero vector and the purity functional. The cited rank-one calculus and the density-operator expansion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), and the definition is read under that assumption. It asserts no dynamics, no measurement, no probability law and no physical interpretation, and it introduces no new assumptions beyond the cited mathematics and that choice hypothesis. In particular, whether a given physical preparation is described by a pure or a mixed state is a question about the model's assignments, not about this definition.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2 and the identical-particle and spin
postulate P6 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) and the radiation
extension postulate
[[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]] in
its clauses (i)-(iv), read in the state vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], the observable vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the sector
vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
and the units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the
Axioms of Countable Choice and of Choice, the choice hypotheses of the cited
Fock space mathematics ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Radiation one-particle space and sectors.** The **transverse one-particle
space** of the radiation sector is
$$\mathfrak h:=\Bigl\{f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3}):\ k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{for almost every }k\Bigr\}$$
with the restricted $L^{2}$ inner product, a separable complex Hilbert space
([[def-hilbert-space]]); its elements are read as **one-photon wave-packet
vectors**. For $n\ge1$ the **$n$-photon sector** is
$\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}=\operatorname{ran}P_{+}^{(n)}\subseteq\mathfrak h^{\otimes n}$
and the **radiation state space** is the bosonic Fock space
$F(\mathfrak h)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}$, whose sector projections
are $\Pi_n$ and whose vacuum is $\Omega=\iota_0(1)$
([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]],
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]]). A **declared
radiation preparation** is a state $\rho\in D(F(\mathfrak h))$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]; a **declared one-photon
preparation** is a preparation whose state is supported in the one-photon
sector, and for a unit $f\in\mathfrak h$ the ray of $\iota_{1}(f)$ is the
one-photon preparation **of wave-packet vector $f$**.

**(c) Modes.** A **mode** of the radiation sector is a nonzero class
$\varphi\in\mathfrak h$ considered up to phase, equivalently the rank-one
orthogonal projection onto $\mathbb C\varphi$; a **declared mode family** is a
finite or countable orthonormal family $(\varphi_{j})$ of $\mathfrak h$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]). For
a unit mode vector $\varphi$ and $z\in\mathbb C$ the vector
$$U_\varphi\psi_z,\qquad \psi_z=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}e_n,$$
is the **mode-coherent preparation vector of label $z$**, and $U_\varphi e_n$
is the **$n$-quanta mode vector**; these are the readings of the transferred
vectors of [[lem-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-isometry]]. A mode vector is a
normalisable wave packet; the sharp-mode label $k$ of the propagation-mode
idealisation is a spectral parameter and is not a state of $\mathfrak h$
([[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]]
clause (c)).

**(d) Assigned observables.** The framework assigns to the radiation sector:

1. the **total number observable** $(N,1)$, the self-adjoint number operator of
   [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]], with domain
   $D(N)=\{\psi:\sum_nn^{2}\|\psi_n\|^{2}<\infty\}$ and read in the
   dimensionless unit $1$ of counted quanta;
2. the **free-field energy observable** $(H_f,\mathrm J)$, the operator
   $H_f=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_{n}$ with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$ and
   $T_{n}\psi=\varepsilon_{n}\psi$, of
   [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]],
   read in joules; its one-particle restriction is the energy multiplier
   $M_{\hbar c|k|}^{\mathfrak h}$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]];
3. for $j\in\{1,2,3\}$ the **total momentum component** $(P_j,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$ is the self-adjoint direct sum of the signed summed multipliers $P_{j,n}$ of [[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-fock-total-momentum]], with $P_{j,0}=0$. In the lemma's exact Euclidean embedding $I_n$ of each symmetric transverse sector, $P_{j,n}$ multiplies by $p_{j,n}(k)=\hbar\sum_i(k_i)_j$ on the maximal domain $\{u:p_{j,n}I_nu\in L^2\}$. Its Fock domain is
   $$D(P_j)=\{\psi:\psi_n\in D(P_{j,n})\text{ for every }n,\ \sum_n\|P_{j,n}\psi_n\|^2<\infty\}.$$
   This is the domain of the sum, without an extra requirement that each individual momentum summand be square integrable. Its spectral PVM is the sectorwise direct sum of the inverse-image indicator multipliers, including the atom at zero on the vacuum. The **one-photon momentum component** is its restriction to sector one, identified with $M_{\hbar k_j}^{\mathfrak h}$ of [[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]]. The postulate assigns these mathematical operators their physical momentum meaning and units.

**(e) Reading of the mode assignments.** In the declared inertial chart the
assignments $\omega(k)=c|k|$ in $\mathrm s^{-1}$, $E(k)=\hbar\omega(k)$ in
$\mathrm J$ and $p(k)=\hbar k$ in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$ of
clause (iii) of the radiation postulate are read through the spectral measures
of clause (d): for a one-photon preparation of unit wave-packet vector
$f\in\mathfrak h$, the **assigned frequency**, **energy** and
**momentum component** laws are the push-forwards of the measure
$\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k$ under $k\mapsto c|k|$,
$k\mapsto\hbar c|k|$ and $k\mapsto\hbar k_{j}$; these laws, and their finite means under the corresponding first-moment conditions, are proved on this page. Sharp
frequency, sharp energy and sharp momentum-component states are not vectors of
$\mathfrak h$; every unit one-photon vector in the corresponding multiplier domain has
finite strictly positive variance in that quantity (clause (d) of
[[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]]).
The push-forward laws themselves exist for every unit $f\in\mathfrak h$, without a moment-domain assumption; all their singleton probabilities vanish by the null level sets in the cited lemma, so they are non-Dirac laws even when finite means or variances do not exist. Thus "photon of energy $\hbar\omega$" names a spectral assignment of the model, not a normalisable state with an exact energy.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (b)-(e) fix the sector assignment and the units. They
assert no detector model, no sampling model, no dynamics, no interaction with
matter, no spontaneous emission and no empirical result; the counting and detection vocabulary is fixed separately on this page. The
identification of a laboratory radiation field with a preparation of
$F(\mathfrak h)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7, and no
Lorentz transformation law for modes or their labels is adopted or claimed.

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1) and the
identical-particle and spin postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] (P6), read with the state
space vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and the
quantities and units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice
hypothesis of the cited tensor construction.

**(b) Declared species and sector.** A **declared species sector** of the model
consists of: a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$, the
**one-particle space** of the species, as assigned in P1; a mass parameter
$m>0$ in kg; a spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and the
internal factor $V_{s}=\mathbb C^{2s+1}$ of P6 clause (ii), with the
**orbital factor** $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ the factor carrying no internal degree of
freedom when the one-particle space is given as a completed product
$H_{\mathrm{sp}}\widehat\otimes V_{s}$; for the massive spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] the one-particle space
is $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$, whose spin components are the
internal factor of P6 clause (ii) in the reading of that definition; a
**statistics choice**
$\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, where $+$ declares the species **bosonic** and $-$
declares it **fermionic**; and, for a charged species, a charge parameter
$q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs. The parameters and the statistics choice are
empirical model assignments with their uncertainties, in the sense of P6
clause (iii); no value and no statistics choice is derived by this definition.

**(c) The $n$-particle sector.** Fix $n\ge1$. The **labelled $n$-particle
space** of the species is the $n$-fold completed tensor power
$H^{\otimes n}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), whose
tensor factors are mathematical labels and not observable particle
identities, equipped with the permutation unitaries $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_n}$
and the sector projections $P_\sigma^{(n)}$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]), where
$P_+^{(n)}$ is the symmetrizing projection and $P_-^{(n)}$ the alternating
projection. The **$n$-particle sector space** of the declared species is
$$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma:=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\ \subseteq\ H^{\otimes n},$$
a closed linear subspace carrying the inner product of $H^{\otimes n}$; on it
every permutation acts by the scalar
$$U_\pi|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}=\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)\, \mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma},\qquad \operatorname{sgn}_+(\pi)=1,\quad \operatorname{sgn}_-(\pi)=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi),$$
by clause (c) of the cited permutation lemma. For $n=1$ one has
$\mathfrak H_1^+=\mathfrak H_1^-=H$.

**(d) Declared sector preparations.** A **declared sector preparation** of $n$
particles of the species is a state of the framework on the sector space,
that is a density operator
$$\rho\in D(\mathfrak H_n^\sigma)$$
in the sense of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and
clause (a) of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], read as the
state assigned to the preparation by P1 clause (iii). A **pure sector
preparation** is a pure state, i.e. the rank-one operator of a unit ray of
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$; a statistical mixture of sector preparations is a
convex combination. The sector is part of the declaration of the species: a
model that declares one statistics choice does not switch it within the same
declaration. When a sector preparation is paired with an operator or a
spectral projection on the labelled space, use its **canonical zero extension**
$\widetilde\rho:=j\rho j^*$, where $j:\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\hookrightarrow
H^{\otimes n}$ is the isometric inclusion and $j^*$ is the orthogonal
projection viewed as a map into the sector. This extension is a density
operator on the labelled space: by clause (a) of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]],
$\rho=\sum_kw_kT_{u_k,u_k}$ in trace norm for an orthonormal family in the
sector and nonnegative weights summing to one. The family $(ju_k)$ is
orthonormal in the labelled space, so the same clause gives the density
$\sum_kw_kT_{ju_k,ju_k}$ there; its action is $j\rho j^*$, since both agree on
the sector and vanish on its orthogonal complement. If the sector is zero,
there is no density preparation of trace one and this convention is vacuous.

**(e) Sector quantities.** Let $A$ be a linear operator on the labelled space
$H^{\otimes n}$ with domain $D(A)$. The model reads $A$ as a **quantity of the
declared sector** only when $A$ **preserves the sector**,
$$P_\sigma^{(n)}D(A)\subseteq D(A),\qquad A\bigl(D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\bigr)\subseteq \mathfrak H_n^\sigma,$$
in which case the **sector restriction** $A_\sigma:=A|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$
with domain $D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ is part of the declaration and is
the quantity actually read on sector preparations; For any bounded $A$, commutation with $P_\sigma^{(n)}$ implies sector
preservation; for bounded self-adjoint $A$ the converse also holds. Indeed,
if such an $A$ preserves the sector, $y$ in its orthogonal complement and
$x$ in the sector satisfy $\langle Ay,x\rangle=\langle y,Ax\rangle=0$,
so the complement is invariant as well; splitting each vector into its two
orthogonal components gives $AP_\sigma^{(n)}=P_\sigma^{(n)}A$. For an arbitrary
bounded operator, invariance alone need not preserve the complement and is
not asserted equivalent to commutation. An
operator that does not preserve the sector is not read on the sector; in
particular no quantity of a single labelled factor is assumed to define a
quantity of the sector unless it preserves it. If $A_\sigma$ is self-adjoint,
its outcome law in a sector preparation is the law of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] read on
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the vocabulary with which the
framework reads the adopted P6 assumptions: they add no assumption to P1 and
P6, and the permutation invariance of sector preparations and of sector
readouts is a conditional consequence proved on this page
([[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-permutation-invariance]]), not a content of
this definition. The definition asserts no spin-statistics theorem, no
dynamics, no measurement instrument and no empirical fact; whether a
laboratory ensemble is described by a declared sector preparation is a tested
identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate
P7, not a consequence of the declaration.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework, for systems in the declared massive-matter sector, the following statements about states and their composition. Assume throughout the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is the choice hypothesis of the mathematical suppliers cited below.

**(i) State space.** To each physical system of the sector the model assigns a complex Hilbert space $H$ that is nonzero and separable: a complex Hilbert space in the sense of [[def-hilbert-space]] which admits a sequence whose range is dense in $H$, so that the hypothesis of [[thm-separable-hilbert-space-has-a-countable-orthonormal-basis]] holds and $H$ has a finite or countable orthonormal basis. The assignment of a Hilbert space to a physical system is a model assumption; the linear structure used to combine descriptions mathematically is not an empirical claim. The physical system to which $H$ is assigned, and the sector in which the assignment is made, are declared with it.

**(ii) Pure preparations.** A **pure preparation** of the system is a unit ray $[\psi]=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a vector $\psi\in H$ with $\|\psi\|=1$; that is, two nonzero vectors describe the same pure preparation exactly when they differ by a nonzero complex factor. The zero vector is not a state and no preparation is assigned to it: the normalization $\|\psi\|=1$ is part of the assignment. The ray allows arbitrary nonzero rescaling; between unit representatives the factor has modulus one and is a **global phase**, which has no observable consequence (P2). The rank-one operator $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] is the density operator associated with the ray of $\psi$.

**(iii) General preparations and mixing.** A general preparation of the system is a **density operator**: a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ on $H$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)). Pure preparations are the special case $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ with $\|\psi\|=1$. A **statistical mixture** of preparations $\rho_{n}$ with weights $w_{n}\ge0$, $\sum_{n}w_{n}=1$, is the trace-norm convergent sum $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ as follows directly in the trace-class Banach space ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]): each density has trace norm one, so $\sum_n\|w_n\rho_n\|_1=1$ gives trace-norm convergence. Every partial sum is positive; operator-norm convergence preserves its nonnegative quadratic forms, and continuity of trace gives $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). Thus the limit is again a density operator, without requiring the components to be orthogonal pure states. The weights are a classical preparation uncertainty and are not amplitudes. Distinct weighted ensembles of pure states may define the same $\rho$.

**(iv) Composition.** Two independent distinguishable subsystems with state spaces $H_{A}$ and $H_{B}$ are composed by the completed Hilbert tensor product $H_{A}\widehat\otimes H_{B}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. Product preparations $\psi_{A}\otimes\psi_{B}$ are the special case of preparations in which each subsystem has its own specified preparation; general composite preparations are linear combinations and mixtures and need not factor. A quantity of subsystem $A$ alone is represented on the composite by an operator of the form $A\otimes I_{B}$ and a quantity of $B$ alone by $I_{A}\otimes B$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] (bounded case; unbounded local operators are treated where they occur). The existence of the completed tensor product is mathematics; the assignment of that product to a composite physical system is the physical assumption here.

**(v) Restrictions that are separate assumptions.** Restrictions of the state space by superselection rules, identical-particle symmetry sectors, and the replacement of the tensor product by more general algebraic structures are not consequences of the clauses above: where such a restriction is used it is adopted separately, and the identical-species sectors are the subject of the postulate P6 of this page.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model within its declared sector. They are not derived from experiment, and they do not assert that a physical system is exactly described by such a Hilbert space; no numerical measurement is recorded. The compatibility of the framework with observation is a question about fully specified models and reported data, in the sense of P7.

The **state space** of $H$ is the set of all density operators on $H$ and is denoted
$$D(H):=\{\rho:\rho\ \text{is a density operator on}\ H\}.$$
An element of $D(H)$ is called a **state** of $H$ in the mathematical sense fixed here.

**Pure states.** A state $\rho\in D(H)$ is **pure** when there is a unit vector $u\in S(H)$ with
$$\rho=T_{u,u},\qquad T_{u,u}x=\langle x,u\rangle u\quad(x\in H),$$
where $T_{u,u}$ is the rank-one operator of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] and $S(H)$ is the unit sphere of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. $$j:R(H)\longrightarrow D(H),\qquad j([\psi]):=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)},$$

$$\widehat\rho(\psi):=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,\psi})},$$

$$U_{n+1}(t,s)=\int_s^t A(r)U_n(r,s)\,dr,$$
where $\int_s^t=-\int_t^s$ when $t<s$. Equivalently, for $s\le t$ these are the **latest-time-left** ordered integrals
$$U_n(t,s)=\Bigl(\frac{-i}{\hbar}\Bigr)^n\int_{s<t_1<\cdots<t_n<t}\mathcal H(t_n)\cdots\mathcal H(t_1)\,dt_1\cdots dt_n,$$

(a) $\|U_n(t,s)\|\le(K|t-s|)^n/n!$ for all $n\ge0$ and all $s,t\in I$.

(b) $U(t,s)=\sum_{n\ge0}U_n(t,s)$ converges in operator norm uniformly on $I\times I$, is jointly norm-continuous, satisfies $U(s,s)=I_H$, and obeys $\|U(t,s)-I_H\|\le e^{K|t-s|}-1$. In particular all original forward-time convergence claims hold.

(c) For every $s,t\in I$,
$$U(t,s)=I_H-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_s^t\mathcal H(r)U(r,s)\,dr.$$

$$\partial_tU(t,s)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\mathcal H(t)U(t,s),\qquad \partial_sU(t,s)=+\frac{i}{\hbar}U(t,s)\mathcal H(s),$$

$$U(t,s)U(s,r)=U(t,r)\qquad(r,s,t\in I).$$

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework, for systems in the declared massive-matter sector, the following statements about states and their composition. Assume throughout the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is the choice hypothesis of the mathematical suppliers cited below.

**(i) State space.** To each physical system of the sector the model assigns a complex Hilbert space $H$ that is nonzero and separable: a complex Hilbert space in the sense of [[def-hilbert-space]] which admits a sequence whose range is dense in $H$, so that the hypothesis of [[thm-separable-hilbert-space-has-a-countable-orthonormal-basis]] holds and $H$ has a finite or countable orthonormal basis. The assignment of a Hilbert space to a physical system is a model assumption; the linear structure used to combine descriptions mathematically is not an empirical claim. The physical system to which $H$ is assigned, and the sector in which the assignment is made, are declared with it.

**(ii) Pure preparations.** A **pure preparation** of the system is a unit ray $[\psi]=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a vector $\psi\in H$ with $\|\psi\|=1$; that is, two nonzero vectors describe the same pure preparation exactly when they differ by a nonzero complex factor. The zero vector is not a state and no preparation is assigned to it: the normalization $\|\psi\|=1$ is part of the assignment. The ray allows arbitrary nonzero rescaling; between unit representatives the factor has modulus one and is a **global phase**, which has no observable consequence (P2). The rank-one operator $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] is the density operator associated with the ray of $\psi$.

**(iii) General preparations and mixing.** A general preparation of the system is a **density operator**: a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ on $H$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)). Pure preparations are the special case $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ with $\|\psi\|=1$. A **statistical mixture** of preparations $\rho_{n}$ with weights $w_{n}\ge0$, $\sum_{n}w_{n}=1$, is the trace-norm convergent sum $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ as follows directly in the trace-class Banach space ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]): each density has trace norm one, so $\sum_n\|w_n\rho_n\|_1=1$ gives trace-norm convergence. Every partial sum is positive; operator-norm convergence preserves its nonnegative quadratic forms, and continuity of trace gives $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). Thus the limit is again a density operator, without requiring the components to be orthogonal pure states. The weights are a classical preparation uncertainty and are not amplitudes. Distinct weighted ensembles of pure states may define the same $\rho$.

**(iv) Composition.** Two independent distinguishable subsystems with state spaces $H_{A}$ and $H_{B}$ are composed by the completed Hilbert tensor product $H_{A}\widehat\otimes H_{B}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. Product preparations $\psi_{A}\otimes\psi_{B}$ are the special case of preparations in which each subsystem has its own specified preparation; general composite preparations are linear combinations and mixtures and need not factor. A quantity of subsystem $A$ alone is represented on the composite by an operator of the form $A\otimes I_{B}$ and a quantity of $B$ alone by $I_{A}\otimes B$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] (bounded case; unbounded local operators are treated where they occur). The existence of the completed tensor product is mathematics; the assignment of that product to a composite physical system is the physical assumption here.

**(v) Restrictions that are separate assumptions.** Restrictions of the state space by superselection rules, identical-particle symmetry sectors, and the replacement of the tensor product by more general algebraic structures are not consequences of the clauses above: where such a restriction is used it is adopted separately, and the identical-species sectors are the subject of the postulate P6 of this page.

They are not derived from experiment, and they do not assert that a physical system is exactly described by such a Hilbert space; no numerical measurement is recorded. The compatibility of the framework with observation is a question about fully specified models and reported data, in the sense of P7.

$$D(H):=\{\rho:\rho\ \text{is a density operator on}\ H\}.$$
An element of $D(H)$ is called a **state** of $H$ in the mathematical sense fixed here.

**Pure states.** A state $\rho\in D(H)$ is **pure** when there is a unit vector $u\in S(H)$ with
$$\rho=T_{u,u},\qquad T_{u,u}x=\langle x,u\rangle u\quad(x\in H),$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\hbar>0$.

**(a) The golden-rule kernel.** For $t>0$ define
$$K_t(x):=\frac1{\hbar^2t}\Bigl|\int_0^te^{ixs/\hbar}\,ds\Bigr|^2,\qquad x\in\mathbb R .$$
Then $K_t$ is continuous, nonnegative and even, and for $x\ne0$
$$K_t(x)=\frac{4\sin^2\bigl(xt/(2\hbar)\bigr)}{x^2t},\qquad K_t(0)=\frac t{\hbar^2};$$
moreover for every $\delta>0$ and every $x$ with $|x|\ge\delta$,
$$K_t(x)\le\frac4{x^2t}\le\frac4{\delta^2t},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}K_t(x)\,dx=\frac{2\pi}{\hbar}.$$

**(b) Approximate identity.** Let $J\in L^1(\mathbb R)$
([[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]) and let $\Delta\in\mathbb R$.
If the representative $J$ is continuous at $\Delta$
([[def-continuity-real]]), then
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\int_{\mathbb R}K_t(x)J(\Delta+x)\,dx=\frac{2\pi}{\hbar}J(\Delta)$$
([[def-limits-at-infinity]]).

**(c) First-order emission coefficient.** Adopt the objects and hypotheses of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]]: $\alpha>0$, the
transverse space $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_\Pi$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
with $\varepsilon(k)=\alpha|k|$, the cutoff $\Lambda>0$, the vectors
$g_1,\dots,g_J\in\mathfrak h$ ($J\ge1$) with
$$\operatorname{supp}g_j\subseteq\{k:\ 0<\varepsilon(k)\le\Lambda\},\qquad \frac{g_j}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\in\mathfrak h,$$
the Hermitian $d\times d$ matrices $H_a,D_1,\dots,D_J$ and the coupling
$\eta_0\in\mathbb R$. Let $v_a,v_b$ be orthonormal eigenvectors of $H_a$ with
$H_av_a=E_av_a$, $H_av_b=E_av_b$, and let $\Delta:=E_a-E_b>0$. Put
$$c_j:=\langle D_jv_a,v_b\rangle\ (\mathbb C^d\text{ inner product}),\qquad M:=\sum_{j=1}^Jc_jg_j\in\mathfrak h,$$
and define the finite Borel measure
$$\nu_b(A):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\mathbf 1_A(\varepsilon(k))\,\|M(k)\|^2\,d^3k, \qquad A\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel},$$
and for $t\ge0$ the amplitude
$$A_b(k,t):=-\frac{i\eta_0}{\hbar}M(k)\int_0^te^{i(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta)s/\hbar}\,ds .$$
Then:

(i) $\nu_b$ is a finite Borel measure on $\mathbb R$ with
$\nu_b(\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda])=0$, and
$$\int_{\mathbb R}f\,d\nu_b=\int_{\mathbb R^3}f(\varepsilon(k))\,\|M(k)\|^2\,d^3k$$
for every Borel $f\ge0$;

(ii) $A_b(\cdot,t)\in\mathfrak h$ for every $t\ge0$, and
for $t>0$,
$$\|A_b(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^2 =\eta_0^2t\int_{\mathbb R}K_t(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_b(E).$$
At $t=0$ the amplitude is zero, so its squared norm is zero; no $K_0$ is used.

(iii) if $\nu_b=J_b\lambda$ for some $J_b\in L^1(\lambda)$ with $J_b=0$
$\lambda$-a.e. on $\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda]$ and the representative $J_b$
continuous at $\Delta$, then for $0<\Delta<\Lambda$
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac1t\|A_b(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^2 =\frac{2\pi\eta_0^2}{\hbar}J_b(\Delta);$$
if instead $\Delta>\Lambda$, then the same limit exists and equals $0$. The
boundary case $\Delta=\Lambda$ is not asserted.

*Motivation and scope.* In the cutoff dipole model of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]] the vector
$A_b(\cdot,t)$ is the explicit single-vertex amplitude with the atom passing
from $v_a$ to $v_b$ and one photon emitted; $\|A_b(\cdot,t)\|^2$ is the
corresponding first-order photon coefficient, and (iii) is the golden-rule
limit of that coefficient divided by $t$. This item computes only the limit of
the explicit coefficient, under the stated hypotheses on the spectral density
$J_b$. It asserts no approximation of the exact model evolution, no all-time or
weak-coupling limit, no Markov property and no exact exponential decay, and it
reports no measurement or empirical rate. The parameter $\hbar$, the coupling
$\eta_0$ and the matrices $D_j$ enter as mathematical normalisation data of the
model; their physical identification is a separate assumption.

inertial chart ([[def-nrqm-framework-inertial-frames]]), the model assigns a
two-dimensional complex internal space, the **transverse polarisation space**

polarisation preparations** of the mode. This assignment is an idealised
manifestation of the abstract Born/state framework on a finite-dimensional
internal factor; it is not a spatial wave function of a massive particle, not a
model of a photon position, and not the massive one-particle Hamiltonian of P5
with mass set to zero: the framework's massive family has no massless
self-adjoint member obtained as $m\downarrow0$
([[cex-nrqm-framework-zero-mass-has-no-self-adjoint-limit]]), and no such limit
is used here.

radiation a **bosonic species** in the sense of P6, whose one-particle space is
the transverse space
$$\mathfrak h:=\Bigl\{f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3}):\ k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{for almost every }k\Bigr\}$$
with the $L^{2}$ inner product; its $n$-particle sector is
$\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}=\operatorname{ran}P_{+}^{(n)}$ and its radiation state
space is the bosonic Fock space $F(\mathfrak h)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}$
([[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]]). The
statistics choice "bosonic" is an empirical model assignment of P6 clause (iii)
and is not derived here; it is motivated by the photon's observed
indistinguishability and integer spin but is adopted, not deduced.

inertial chart, each free mode label $k\in\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$ is
assigned the **angular frequency** $\omega(k):=c|k|$ in $\mathrm s^{-1}$, the
**photon energy** $E(k):=\hbar\omega(k)=\hbar c|k|$ in joules and the
**photon momentum** $p(k):=\hbar k$ in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$,
where $c=2{,}99792458\times10^{8}\ \mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$ and
$\hbar=h/(2\pi)>0$ in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$ have the SI values of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (c). Ordinary frequency is
$\nu(k)=\omega(k)/(2\pi)$ in hertz. These are separate quantum-radiation model
assignments: they are neither consequences of classical Maxwell theory nor
consequences of the special-relativistic framework, and no Lorentz
transformation law for the mode label $k$, for $\omega(k)$ or for the
polarisation pair is adopted or claimed; the extension does not assert Galilean
covariance of the radiation sector, and it does not identify the massless
Lorentz representations of the photon with the representations of the spatial
rotation group used in P6.

**(iv) Free-field observables.** The model assigns the total free-field energy
observable $H_f=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_{n}$ with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$ and

self-adjointness are the mathematics of

and [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]] for energy and
number, and [[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-fock-total-momentum]] for total

[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]].

number and energy *statistics* require a declared detector model in the sense
of P2 and P7, which this postulate does not supply; a prescribed classical
electromagnetic field does not by itself yield photon counting or vacuum
spontaneous emission. No light-matter Hamiltonian, no dipole coupling, no
emission or absorption process and no recoil model is asserted here; the
absorption/stimulated-emission branch with a finite-level dipole coupling and
the quantised-mode emission construction are separate model assumptions for
the later pair on light-matter and spectral transitions. The relation of a
laboratory field, polariser or detector to this model is a tested
identification with uncertainty under P7, not a consequence of the postulate.

non-relativistic in its matter sector: it adds external free radiation modes to

matter, antiparticles, pair creation, covariant local field dynamics and full

disguised as solved core prerequisites; they require a named field-theory
destination. No position wave function of the photon satisfying the massive
Schrödinger equation is introduced.

laboratory field, polariser or detector is exactly described by the model is
made by this item.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework, for systems in the declared massive-matter sector, the following statements about states and their composition. Assume throughout the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is the choice hypothesis of the mathematical suppliers cited below.

**(i) State space.** To each physical system of the sector the model assigns a complex Hilbert space $H$ that is nonzero and separable: a complex Hilbert space in the sense of [[def-hilbert-space]] which admits a sequence whose range is dense in $H$, so that the hypothesis of [[thm-separable-hilbert-space-has-a-countable-orthonormal-basis]] holds and $H$ has a finite or countable orthonormal basis. The assignment of a Hilbert space to a physical system is a model assumption; the linear structure used to combine descriptions mathematically is not an empirical claim. The physical system to which $H$ is assigned, and the sector in which the assignment is made, are declared with it.

**(ii) Pure preparations.** A **pure preparation** of the system is a unit ray $[\psi]=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a vector $\psi\in H$ with $\|\psi\|=1$; that is, two nonzero vectors describe the same pure preparation exactly when they differ by a nonzero complex factor. The zero vector is not a state and no preparation is assigned to it: the normalization $\|\psi\|=1$ is part of the assignment. The ray allows arbitrary nonzero rescaling; between unit representatives the factor has modulus one and is a **global phase**, which has no observable consequence (P2). The rank-one operator $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] is the density operator associated with the ray of $\psi$.

**(iii) General preparations and mixing.** A general preparation of the system is a **density operator**: a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ on $H$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)). Pure preparations are the special case $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ with $\|\psi\|=1$. A **statistical mixture** of preparations $\rho_{n}$ with weights $w_{n}\ge0$, $\sum_{n}w_{n}=1$, is the trace-norm convergent sum $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ as follows directly in the trace-class Banach space ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]): each density has trace norm one, so $\sum_n\|w_n\rho_n\|_1=1$ gives trace-norm convergence. Every partial sum is positive; operator-norm convergence preserves its nonnegative quadratic forms, and continuity of trace gives $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). Thus the limit is again a density operator, without requiring the components to be orthogonal pure states. The weights are a classical preparation uncertainty and are not amplitudes. Distinct weighted ensembles of pure states may define the same $\rho$.

**(iv) Composition.** Two independent distinguishable subsystems with state spaces $H_{A}$ and $H_{B}$ are composed by the completed Hilbert tensor product $H_{A}\widehat\otimes H_{B}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. Product preparations $\psi_{A}\otimes\psi_{B}$ are the special case of preparations in which each subsystem has its own specified preparation; general composite preparations are linear combinations and mixtures and need not factor. A quantity of subsystem $A$ alone is represented on the composite by an operator of the form $A\otimes I_{B}$ and a quantity of $B$ alone by $I_{A}\otimes B$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] (bounded case; unbounded local operators are treated where they occur). The existence of the completed tensor product is mathematics; the assignment of that product to a composite physical system is the physical assumption here.

**(v) Restrictions that are separate assumptions.** Restrictions of the state space by superselection rules, identical-particle symmetry sectors, and the replacement of the tensor product by more general algebraic structures are not consequences of the clauses above: where such a restriction is used it is adopted separately, and the identical-species sectors are the subject of the postulate P6 of this page.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model within its declared sector. They are not derived from experiment, and they do not assert that a physical system is exactly described by such a Hilbert space; no numerical measurement is recorded. The compatibility of the framework with observation is a question about fully specified models and reported data, in the sense of P7.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following statements about sharp and unsharp real-valued quantities. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The latter is the explicit hypothesis used to obtain the spectral PVM of a general self-adjoint operator from [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] in clause (ii); consumers invoking this construction inherit it.

**(i) Sharp observables.** An **ideal sharp real-valued quantity** (observable) of a system with state space $H$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), together with a declared unit in which its real spectral coordinate is read; the unit is part of the assignment, and no numerical value of the coordinate is asserted by the assignment. Symmetry of $A$ on a small domain is not sufficient for self-adjointness, and the domain is a declared part of the observable.

**(ii) Spectral probability.** Let $E_{A}$ be the spectral projection-valued measure of the self-adjoint operator $A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$ and a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ the **probability of the outcome in $B$** is
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_{A}(B)\bigr),\qquad\text{and for a pure preparation }[\psi]\text{ it is }\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}.$$
By clause (b) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] the assignment $B\mapsto\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$ is a probability measure on the Borel sets ([[def-probability-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). It is the general form of the Born rule adopted here.

**(iii) Nature of the outcome law.** The probability law is a measure, not necessarily a density with respect to Lebesgue measure and not necessarily a finite or countable sum of point masses: a self-adjoint operator with continuous spectrum ordinarily has no normalizable eigenvector at a point of its continuous spectrum, so an "exact value" of a continuum quantity is not represented by a normalized state. An ideal point value is an idealization; a real detector reports a finite-resolution outcome, that is, the probability of a declared Borel set $B$ such as a bin, and the recorded-event probability is that of (ii) for the bin, not the value of a density at a point.

**(iv) Unsharp finite outcomes.** Outcomes of a finite-resolution apparatus with finitely many channels are described, when the idealization uses bounded effects, by a finite family $(F_{a})_{a=1}^{p}$ of bounded operators with $0\le F_{a}\le I$ in the quadratic-form order and $\sum_{a}F_{a}=I$ ([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (a)), the **outcome probabilities** being $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})\ge0$, $\sum_{a}p_{a}=1$ by clause (b) of the same lemma. This unsharp extension is an operational description tied to an apparatus model; it is not obtained from the sharp observable by mathematical manipulation alone, and the effects alone do not determine what happens to the state after the outcome (P3).

**(v) Moments are a separate matter.** Statements about the mean, variance or higher moments of the outcome law require the corresponding integrability of $t\mapsto t^{n}$ against $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ and are not part of this postulate; where they are used they are stated with their hypotheses. In particular the existence of $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$ for an unbounded $A$ is not asserted.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model. They assert nothing about which quantities of a concrete apparatus are sharp, about the physical mechanism producing an outcome or about the completeness of the description; a laboratory record is a classical event whose relation to the model is a tested identification with uncertainty, in the sense of P7.

$$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),\qquad U(t+s)=U(t)U(s),\quad U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1},$$

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework, for systems in the declared massive-matter sector, the following statements about states and their composition. Assume throughout the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is the choice hypothesis of the mathematical suppliers cited below.

**(i) State space.** To each physical system of the sector the model assigns a complex Hilbert space $H$ that is nonzero and separable: a complex Hilbert space in the sense of [[def-hilbert-space]] which admits a sequence whose range is dense in $H$, so that the hypothesis of [[thm-separable-hilbert-space-has-a-countable-orthonormal-basis]] holds and $H$ has a finite or countable orthonormal basis. The assignment of a Hilbert space to a physical system is a model assumption; the linear structure used to combine descriptions mathematically is not an empirical claim. The physical system to which $H$ is assigned, and the sector in which the assignment is made, are declared with it.

**(ii) Pure preparations.** A **pure preparation** of the system is a unit ray $[\psi]=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a vector $\psi\in H$ with $\|\psi\|=1$; that is, two nonzero vectors describe the same pure preparation exactly when they differ by a nonzero complex factor. The zero vector is not a state and no preparation is assigned to it: the normalization $\|\psi\|=1$ is part of the assignment. The ray allows arbitrary nonzero rescaling; between unit representatives the factor has modulus one and is a **global phase**, which has no observable consequence (P2). The rank-one operator $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] is the density operator associated with the ray of $\psi$.

**(iii) General preparations and mixing.** A general preparation of the system is a **density operator**: a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ on $H$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)). Pure preparations are the special case $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ with $\|\psi\|=1$. A **statistical mixture** of preparations $\rho_{n}$ with weights $w_{n}\ge0$, $\sum_{n}w_{n}=1$, is the trace-norm convergent sum $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ as follows directly in the trace-class Banach space ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]): each density has trace norm one, so $\sum_n\|w_n\rho_n\|_1=1$ gives trace-norm convergence. Every partial sum is positive; operator-norm convergence preserves its nonnegative quadratic forms, and continuity of trace gives $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). Product preparations $\psi_{A}\otimes\psi_{B}$ are the special case of preparations in which each subsystem has its own specified preparation; general composite preparations are linear combinations and mixtures and need not factor. A quantity of subsystem $A$ alone is represented on the composite by an operator of the form $A\otimes I_{B}$ and a quantity of $B$ alone by $I_{A}\otimes B$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] (bounded case; unbounded local operators are treated where they occur). The existence of the completed tensor product is mathematics; the assignment of that product to a composite physical system is the physical assumption here.
